wins.text: Full year net income up nearly 40% to $12.7 billion; RoTCE improved over 200 bps to 7% for the year
Markets had its highest Q4 revenue in a decade, up 36% YoY; Equities up 26% for the year, a record; Banking fees up 42% for the full year with ~50 bps of share gained
Board authorized a $20 billion share repurchase program; returned nearly $7 billion in capital to common shareholders in 2024
Services delivered record full year revenues of $19.6 billion, up 9%, with RoTCE of 26%; gained share in both TTS and Security Services
Wealth Q4 revenue up 20%, pretax margin of 21%, net new investment asset inflows of $42 billion, up 40% YoY; Citigold Asia particularly strong

risks.text: 2026 RoTCE target cut to 10%-11% from prior 11%-12%, driven by elevated transformation and technology investment needs, particularly in data and regulatory reporting
Card net credit losses expected to creep toward the high end of guidance ranges: branded cards ~4%, retail services ~6.28%; provision builds expected to continue on volume growth
Expenses remain elevated; 2025 expenses guided to only slightly below $53.8 billion, with $600 million repositioning charge still embedded; path to sub-60% efficiency ratio pushed beyond 2026
Banamex IPO timeline uncertain, dependent on regulatory approvals and market conditions; could slip into 2026, delaying RWA release and capital benefit
Macro uncertainty around tariffs, tax policy, non-U.S. rate cuts, FX translation, and potential card late fee regulation create headwinds to NII and revenue growth

guidance_items.detail: 2025 revenues guided to $83.5B-$84.5B, ~3%-4% growth YoY, above prior medium-term 4%-5% growth framework baseline
2026 RoTCE target lowered to 10%-11% from prior 11%-12%
Targeting sub-60% efficiency ratio as firm exits 2026; positive operating leverage expected every year
NII ex-Markets expected up modestly (~2%-3%) in 2025; tailwinds from loan/deposit volume growth and portfolio repricing partially offset by rate cuts and FX

2025 expenses expected slightly below $53.8B; 2026 expenses targeted below $53B, driven by stranded cost reduction, lower severance (~$300M normalized vs. $600M guided for 2025), and productivity savings

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Pace and specific timing of the $20 billion buyback program beyond Q1 2025 — management did not proactively address quarterly cadence or milestones for accelerating repurchases
Structural low RoTCE of U.S. Personal Banking (below cost of capital) and its loan-heavy, deposit-light balance sheet relative to peers — not addressed in prepared remarks
Specific magnitude of technology and transformation spend increases embedded in 2025 and 2026 expense guidance — management disclosed directional increase but no dollar figures in prepared remarks
